method.summary: How often does this agent's own stopping rule name a winner that is not there? The rule as written and used: at a scheduled read, stop when one arm's P(best) is at least 0.95 and both arms have at least 100 assignments; reads happened at every wake, about three a day, against a 30-day horizon. Monte Carlo in one dependency-free Node script with a fixed seed, so every row re-runs to the same number: the sampleSize field carries the smallest replicate count behind any row, 1200 (rows vary: the false-decision rows run 1500 and the validation anchor 4000), and every row states its own replicate count and 95 percent interval, because at 1200 replicates the binomial margin near one half is about 2.8 points, and two independent seeded batches of the same configuration returning 42.9 and 43.3 is agreement rather than precision. Arrival is modelled Poisson at the measured assignment rate, both arms converting at 5 percent unless a lift is stated. The probability function is copied verbatim out of the product's ab-test-calculator.html, so a disagreement with these rows is a disagreement with the shipped calculator. Validation anchor, run and printed first: with ONE look at n=3000 per arm and no true difference, the rule must fire at 2(1-t) = 10.0 percent; it measures 10.3, and if that row fails every other row is void. The arithmetic is not what failed here. The instrument is: a threshold is a property of the statistics plus the read cadence, and this specification named the threshold in one section and the cadence in another. Baselines in this file are the references the rule would have to beat to support the claim, not the values the simulation expected: 5 percent is the error budget a 0.95 threshold is read as promising, and 80 percent is the conventional power target. Rows that describe rather than test carry no baseline, because the catalog rightly ignores those when it decides whether this evidence supports the claim or contradicts it.
method.dataset: Arrival rates from GA4 property sessions for livevariant.ai and prior.livevariant.ai, 30 days to 2026-09-23 (1.13 and 3.93 assignments/day) and ~64/day measured on the third-party page of the agent's second test; all decision outcomes from the seeded simulation.
